payload.author: recovery-worker
evidence: Deck build/recovery/decks/fill-rect-v2.out: inplace-add, assign-add, readback-2only and plain-swapped candidates all fail with 18 diffs at offsets 26-49 (correct register allocation, hoisted adds); readback-1only fails with 16 diffs at offsets 8,15,22,... (adds positioned but loads reordered from byte 8).

Deck build/recovery/decks/fill-rect-v3.out: ptr-first-only and ptr-second-only fail with 40 diffs (the mixed direct/pointer stores restructure the reload block); ptr-sum-stores fails with the plain 18-diff signature.

The two adds are the image's only instructions between the store pairs (0x0062AB2A store [ecx+0x58C], 0x0062AB30 store [ecx+0x590], 0x0062AB36 add edx,edi, 0x0062AB38 add eax,esi, 0x0062AB3A store [ecx+0x594], 0x0062AB40 store [ecx+0x598]); in the compiled plain form both adds precede the first store, which is what moves every byte in the 26-49 window.

After adopting plain sums family-wide, decode_fli_copy_trans fails at 18 diffs (was 19) and decode_fli_copy at 37 (was 35, its additional offsets 74-85 in the row loop predate this change and remain unexplained) - build/recovery/decks/check-after-rect-plain.out; the trade and both measured shapes are documented in the comment above Flic::fill in src/flic.cpp.
payload.hypothesis: No idiomatic C++ spelling reproduces the image's add scheduling inside the rect block: the image stores rect0 and rect1, then computes the two sums in place between the store pairs (`add edx,edi`/`add eax,esi` at 0x0062AB36-0x0062AB39, sums landing in x's and y's registers) before storing rect2/rect3. Thirteen measured spellings fall into exactly two failure shapes under both flag sets: every plain-sum spelling (including `x += width`, `x = x + width`, `width + x`) lets VC6 hoist both adds above the stores (18 diffs at offsets 26-49), and every read-back spelling (`rect[2] = rect[0] + width`) keeps the adds near the stores but reorders the first three member loads (16 diffs starting at offsets 8/15/22) and still hoists the second add above the rect1 store; routing only some of the four stores through the pointer restructures the reload block entirely (40 diffs). The plain form was kept as the structurally closest and most idiomatic spelling; the hoisted adds are the family's residual mismatch.
